title: Low-bit fidelity vs throughput matrix: INT4/INT8/FP16 benchmarking harness
creator: Marina Ortega
description: Goal: build a robust, reproducible harness that measures throughput (tokens/sec), tail latency (p95/p99), and quality deltas for three quantization tiers (FP16, INT8, INT4) across representative production traces and synthetic stress patterns. Deliverables: (1) CI-friendly job definitions that run on Dedicated and Hosted-like instance pools, (2) a comparison matrix that correlates tokens/sec vs quality (embedding cosine, LM logp delta, and automated hallucination score), (3) regression detection rules that integrate with Sentry + console alerts, and (4) a cookbook for engineers to add new models and workloads.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Harness executes head-to-head runs for FP16/INT8/INT4 on a minimum of 5 models (small/med/large families) and produces a reproducible CSV matrix.
2) Tokens/sec and p95 computed across 5 realistic trace shards and 3 synthetic extremes (burst, long-context, short-prompt).
3) Quality delta computed via embedding cosine similarity to FP16 baseline, generation log-likelihood delta, and a hallucination proxy; thresholds for acceptable drop defined per-model.
4) Regression rule: automated CI failure when tokens/sec decreases >10% at P95 with no corresponding quality improvement, or when quality drops >2% absolute on embedding similarity.
5) Results surfaced to Console dashboard and a GitHub summary comment on PRs touching quantization kernels.
test_matrix: Quant tiers: FP16 (baseline), INT8 symmetric, INT8 asymmetric, INT4 (per-channel where supported)
Workloads: production traces (chat, instruction), long context (8k+), short burst (1-32 tokens), and throughput stress (concurrent streams)
Metrics: tokens/sec (mean/std), p50/p95/p99 latency, memory usage, KV cache hit impact, embedding cosine vs baseline, logp delta, hallucination proxy rate
methodology: Runs are deterministic where possible: fixed seeds, pinned kernels, and identical batching policies. Use two runner types: (A) Dedicated-sim nodes (same GPU class as dedicated customers) for throughput numbers; (B) Hosted emulation nodes to validate fallback routing behavior. Each config runs 10 trials and we report median and interquartile ranges. Use production-sampled traces (anonymized) plus synthetic amplifiers to exercise long-tail behavior.
regression_detection_plan: 1) Ingest benchmark CSVs into the bench-postgres + metrics pipeline. 2) Calculate delta vs the FP16 baseline and last-green run. 3) Apply dynamic thresholds: if tokens/sec drop >10% at median or p95 and quality unchanged/worse => trigger failure. If quality drop >2% absolute for embedding similarity or >0.5 nats average logp delta => mark as quality regression. 4) Auto-file ENG ticket with summary and attach raw payload; notify owners via #bench-alerts. 5) Provide automatic revert suggestion for quant kernel PRs when regression correlates with a single PR.
open_questions: Do we treat INT4 as 'experimental' in the console or expose it as a selectable profile for customers?
Should per-channel quantization be enabled by default for 13B+ models or gated behind kernel-level feature flags?
What hallucination proxy threshold aligns with customer expectations — 1% or 3%? We need product guidance.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Non-determinism across GPU microcode causes noisy p95 readings. Mitigation: pin driver/kernel versions and run larger trial counts.
Risk: Production traces contain golden prompts that leak PII. Mitigation: anonymize, use sampling and privacy filters before import.
Risk: INT4 outcomes vary widely per model. Mitigation: add model-specific acceptance thresholds and mark INT4 as experimental in alerts.
implementation_steps: 1) Define job YAMLs for Dedicated and Hosted-emulation pools (Ravi)
2) Implement runner + measurement SDK where tokens/sec, p95, and quality proxies are computed in a single pass (Alex)
3) Wire results into bench-postgres and a console ingestion job (Marina)
4) Add regression-detection lambda that compares to last-green and files tickets (SRE)
5) Create dashboard with matrix visualizations and per-model drilldowns (Design/Console)
6) Run full sweep on 5 models and produce PR with results and recommendations (team)
7) Post-mortem and decision on INT4 exposure to customers
comments: 2025-02-18 Marina Ortega: Drafted initial scope and acceptance criteria. Decided to include embedding similarity as primary quality metric because it correlates with retrieval and hallucination proxies.
2025-02-20 Ravi Patel: Agreed on 3 runner types. Suggest we support asymmetric INT8 as a separate column to capture encoder bias effects.
2025-02-27 Alex Novak: Prototype runner implemented. Early numbers show INT8 ~1.6x tokens/sec vs FP16 on A100 with minimal embedding delta on smaller models.
2025-03-03 Design review (Priya Shah): Dashboard mockups look good, request to include an explainer for per-model acceptance boundaries.
2025-03-05 Marina Ortega: Updated estimate and added S3 path for raw runs. Next: schedule dedicated pool runs week of 2025-03-10.
